title: Amortize git fork+exec with a persistent cat-file --batch process
description:
Every git read in thegn is a fresh `fork`+`exec`. Add process reuse behind the existing `util::git_out` chokepoint.

**Payoff:** reduces spawn overhead without adding a single crate — the only shell-out reduction that does not trade dependencies for spawns.

**Estimate:** 1–2 days.

## Measured

On this repo, 2026-09-15 (hyperfine, `-N`, 3 warmup runs):

* `git rev-parse HEAD` — **1.9 ms ± 0.2 ms** \[user 0.6, system 1.1\]
* `git status --porcelain=v2 --branch` — **25.8 ms ± 1.0 ms**

So \~1.9 ms is the **floor** for any git invocation: fork, exec, config load, repo discovery. At 16 ms frame budget, one trivial git spawn is \~12% of a frame. A path touching N worktrees pays N × 1.9 ms before git does any useful work.

A grep for `cat-file` / `--batch` across production code returns only gpg usage — **there is no process reuse anywhere today.**

## Volume

| Helper | Production sites | Files |
| -- | -- | -- |
| `util::git_out` | 77 | 39 |
| `util::git_cmd` | 34 | 21 |
| `util::git_ok` | 25 | 8 |
| `GitLoc::git_command` | 14 | 10 |

## Approach

A long-lived `git cat-file --batch` (and/or `--batch-check`) per repo, owned behind `util::git_out`, so object reads become a pipe write + read instead of a process spawn.

Constraints from CLAUDE.md that this must respect:

* **Never on the event loop.** These already run off-loop; keep it that way, and do not let a stalled child block a caller.
* **0% idle.** A parked child process must not generate wakeups. It sits on a blocking read — verify with `THEGN_PERF=1` that wake-source attribution is unchanged.
* The process needs a lifecycle: lazy start, restart-on-crash, bounded idle lifetime, and cleanup on detach. A dead child must degrade to a plain spawn, never error.
* **Scope honestly:** this only helps object reads (`cat-file`, `rev-parse`-shaped queries). It does **not** help `status`, `diff`, or anything porcelain — those are where the 25.8 ms lives, and they need a different fix (or `gix`, see <issue id="9d3b7179-5f46-47c1-ae15-fce6ec0ef9be" href="https://linear.app/blakeashley/issue/THE-673/benchmark-gix-native-diff-against-the-git-cli-before-keeping-75-crates">THE-673</issue>).

## Prior art in-tree

This codebase already reduces spawns in two ways, and the new work should match those patterns rather than invent a third:

* `BranchSet::load` (`thegn-core/src/worktree.rs`) — its comment notes collision checks are now "pure lookups (the old per-candidate probing ran two subprocesses per attempt)". N spawns → 2 spawns + an in-memory set.
* `panel_header_cache` + `hydrate::glyph_cache` — last-known-good caches so a failed git read does not re-spawn next frame.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Object reads go through a reused process; measured before/after on a repo with many worktrees.
- [ ] A killed or crashed child degrades to a plain spawn with no user-visible error.
- [ ] `THEGN_PERF=1` shows no new wake source and no idle-ratio regression.
- [ ] No new dependency.
- [ ] Child processes are reaped on detach — no orphans after the UI exits.
- [ ] `cargo nextest run --workspace` green; `just lint` green.

## Out of scope

`GitLoc::git_command` for remote (ssh/provider) locs — batching across an ssh hop is a different problem. Local only.
